q-78598.name: Question 1
q-78598.problem:
Which of the following integers belong to the residue class $[6]_{9}?$

I. $-12$

II. $3$

III. $24$
q-78598.worked_solution:
The residue class $[6]_{9}$ consists of the elements that are congruent to $6$ modulo $9.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[6]_{9} & =\{x\in Z\,|\,x≡6\,(\text{mod}\,9)\} \\  & =\{x\in Z\,|\,x=6+9k,\,k\in Z\} \\  & =\{6+9k\,|\,k\in Z\} \\  & =\{…,\,6-2\cdot 9,\,6-9,\,6,\,6+9,\,6+2\cdot 9,\,…\} \\  & =\{…,-12,-3,6,15,24,…\}.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that $-12$ and $24$ belong to $[6]_{9},$ while $3$ does not.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".

q-78605.name: Question 6
q-78605.problem:
Which of the following residue classes modulo $9$ contain the integer $-6?$

I. $[2]_{9}$

II. $[-3]_{9}$

III. $[3]_{9}$
q-78605.worked_solution:
We have $-6\in [a]_{9}$ if 

$$
-6≡a\,(\text{mod}\,9).
$$

Let's now consider each of the given equivalence classes.

- $-6\notin [2]_{9}$ because $-6≢2\,(\text{mod}\,9)$ $\,\times $

- $-6\notin [-3]_{9}$ because $-6≢-3\,(\text{mod}\,9)$ $\,\times $

- $-6\in [3]_{9}$ because $-6≡3\,(\text{mod}\,9)$ $\,✓$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".
